about.title: Los Gatos Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Los Gatos residents run into defective products in ordinary ways — a faulty bike component on a ride along the foothills, a malfunctioning kitchen appliance in a Blossom Hill Road home, or defective auto parts that fail during the Friday afternoon crush along SR-17. California law gives injured people an advantage here: strict liability means you generally don't have to prove a manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. That defect might be in the design, in how the item was manufactured, or in inadequate warnings or instructions. Liability can reach the manufacturer, the distributor, or the retailer who sold it. If a defective product hurt you or someone in your family in Los Gatos, holding onto the item and any packaging matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself — we simply connect you with an independent attorney, at no cost, who can look at what happened and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Los Gatos Claimants

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Carelessness
items.desc: Under California's strict liability standard, showing the product itself was defective and caused your injury is generally enough — you don't need to dig into how careful or careless the manufacturer was.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which matters when a defective product moved through several hands before it reached a Los Gatos home or store shelf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Because these cases often turn on physical or design evidence, keeping the product, its packaging, and any manuals intact gives an attorney the strongest starting point to evaluate a design, manufacturing, or warning defect.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. California's strict liability rule for defective products generally requires showing the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving the manufacturer failed to use reasonable care. An attorney can review your specific situation to confirm how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, along with any packaging, receipts, or instructions. This physical evidence is often central to evaluating a design, manufacturing, or warning defect claim, so avoid repairing or discarding it before an attorney has a chance to look at it.

items.question: Does it matter that this happened in Los Gatos specifically?
items.answer: California product liability law applies statewide, so the core legal standards are the same whether the incident happened near SR-85, on Los Gatos Boulevard, or elsewhere in Santa Clara County. That said, local details — like where you bought the product or where the injury occurred — can help an attorney understand the full picture of your claim.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent attorney in our network. Attorneys typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
